title: The Mirror-Word Mystery
subtitle: Palindromes — live with your Enrichment group

learningFocus.summary: Students practise identifying palindromes — words that read the same forwards and backwards — a playful entry point into letter-pattern recognition, spelling and word structure that strengthens phonics and vocabulary skills. Working live alongside their Enrichment group, they test words in a 3D Mirror Chamber, connect the idea to their own names and everyday words, and celebrate each other's discoveries with positive, teacher-safe reactions.

orient.objective: Today you will learn to spot a Mirror Word (a palindrome) — a word that reads exactly the same forwards and backwards.
orient.realLife: Mirror Words are hiding everywhere — in names like Anna and Hannah, in everyday words like noon and pop, and even in silly sentences! Spotting them turns you into a word detective wherever you look.
orient.courseLink: This is today's Primary Enrichment English session — a live, playful practice of a spelling pattern that sharpens the way you read and think about words.
successCriteria: I can explain what makes a word a Mirror Word (palindrome).
I can test a word by reading it forwards and backwards to check.
I can spot Mirror Words in real names and everyday words.

predict.prompt: Quick guess before we start: which of these is a Mirror Word?

explain.prompt: Why does LEVEL look exactly the same forwards and backwards?

options.label: Because its letters are arranged so the first half mirrors the second half around a middle letter
Because it has exactly five letters
Because it starts with a capital letter

apply.prompt: Which of these is a real name that is also a Mirror Word?
